content: The happiness of your life depends upon the quality of your thoughts.
author: Marcus Aurelius
story:
Most of the anxiety and exhaustion we experience does not come from events themselves, but from the relentless internal commentary we run on top of them. Marcus Aurelius noticed that circumstances are neutral facts—rain falls, plans get disrupted, people behave selfishly. The suffering begins only when our ego attaches a catastrophic story to what happened.

By taking ownership of your own judgments, you reclaim your inner fortress. You cannot control what happens around you, but nothing can force you to interpret it as your ruin.
reflectionPrompt: Identify a source of friction in your day. How much of your stress comes from the actual event, and how much comes from the story you're telling yourself about it?

practicalInsight: When friction strikes, separate the raw event from your reaction to it. You have the sovereign freedom to choose calm over panic.
originalQuote: The happiness of your life depends upon the quality of your thoughts: therefore, guard accordingly, and take care that you entertain no notions unsuitable to virtue and reasonable nature.
